messages:
jess_se: FYI received from Acme customer — during a large bulk ingest around their local midnight they started getting 429s and their org credits dropped to 0 mid-run. They say they hadn’t hit the monthly cap earlier in the day. Repro details pasted below.

mike_supp: Can you paste the raw error responses they saw and the timeframe (UTC)? Also did this happen during any Redwood maintenance/infra window? :eyes:

jess_se: Customer timeline: started bulk job 2024-11-28T23:45:00-08:00, saw 429s at ~2024-11-29T00:05:00-08:00. They attached this header from one request: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1690742400
X-Quota-Window: monthly
{"error":"quota_exhausted","message":"monthly credits exhausted for org"}
```

lina_infra: Thanks. X-RateLimit-Reset epoch 1690742400 -> that resolves to 2023-07-30 00:00:00 UTC, but the customer provided local timezone timestamps. Two things to check: (1) whether the tenant has org-level timezone configured (affects UI display) and (2) whether their bulk ingest had many parallel retries that double-count tokens due to client retry storm.

mike_supp: Also note there was a short infra maintenance at 2024-11-29T00:00:30Z (rolling kernel upgrade on a small subset of edge proxies). opsbot should have posted the maintenance announcement to #incidents — @opsbot, can you confirm the affected region and if that impacted quota propagation?

opsbot: maintenance: rolling edge-proxy update started at 2024-11-29T00:00:30Z, regions: us-west-2 (partial), impact: brief reconnects and 502/504s for in-flight connections. No planned quota changes.

lina_infra: Quick analysis: two likely contributors here — quota exhaustion plus a propagation/visibility lag. Sequence plausible: customer hits monthly cap around 00:04 UTC, our quota engine marks tenant exhausted and enforces 429s. Shortly after, the rolling upgrade caused some edge reconnections; client SDKs retried aggressively (parallel requests), which accelerated token burn. UI might show "refilled" or still-zero depending on refresh timing and tenant timezone mapping.

jess_se: Customer insists they were ~10% under monthly before starting job. Is it possible the billing/top-off did not happen because their plan change/proration occurred earlier?

billing-bot: billing: last invoice/proration for tenant org-acme processed 2024-11-01T12:15:00Z. No manual top-up recorded since. Current on-plan: Standard monthly.

mike_supp: Two actionables for support: 1) ask customer for a single request id (x-request-id) from a failing call so we can trace exact token accounting; 2) ask for client SDK logs to confirm retry behaviour (concurrency and backoff). I can request an exception/top-up if this was a clear platform/propagation error.

jess_se: Provided request id: req_0a9b3c. Customer attached SDK log snippet showing they spawn 12 worker threads with no jitter for parallel uploads. They also show 3x retries within 2s for some requests.

lina_infra: That makes it clear — concurrency + retries likely produced a much higher token draw than expected. Also the X-RateLimit-Reset header in the snippet is monthly-window-based and ties to the org's monthly boundary (UTC-based in backend). If customer is on a local midnight mental model, that mismatch causes confusion: we reset monthly at 00:00 UTC, not tenant-local-midnight.

mike_supp: Proposed reply to customer: explain UTC reset, ask for x-request-id + SDK logs, offer temporary one-off credit top-up while we investigate, and recommend client-side backoff/jitter for bulk jobs. Also mention we’ll audit token accounting for req_0a9b3c. Thoughts? :+1:

jess_se: Sounds good. I'll draft the message. Include a sample snippet to recommend exponential backoff and limiting concurrency. Example we can share: 

```
# recommended concurrency/backoff pseudocode
max_workers = 4
for task in tasks:
  retry_count = 0
  while retry_count < 5:
    try:
      send_request()
      break
    except TransientError:
      sleep(exp_backoff(retry_count) + random_jitter())
      retry_count += 1
```

lina_infra: I'll run a quick audit on req_0a9b3c and the tenant's token ledger; expect a follow-up within 2 hours. If we find platform double-counting or a propagation bug during the rolling upgrade, escalate for reimbursement/top-up automatically.

mike_supp: Thanks — add note to thread when audit complete and whether we need to issue a manual credit.

jess_se: Customer reply: "Thanks, we'll send the SDK logs and request ids now. Appreciate temporary top-up while you investigate." :pray:

lina_infra: Audit update (2024-11-29T02:10Z): ledger shows the org hit the cap at 2024-11-29T00:04:12Z UTC. Token consumption pattern shows bursts matching parallel workers and retries, no evidence of double-counting on our side. Propagation lag was <7s; rolling upgrade did not alter quota enforcement.

mike_supp: Closing steps: (1) Offer one-time courtesy credit to cover burst overage and avoid customer disruption (we recommend 10% of their monthly bucket as a gesture). (2) Share best-practice concurrency/backoff guidance. (3) Notify product docs team to add clearer note about UTC boundary vs tenant-local expectations.

jess_se: Customer accepted courtesy credit and implemented max_workers=4 + jitter. They reported no further 429s on a retry of the job. Closing from support side. :white_check_mark:
